candidates.rationale: Ranks how large today's return is relative to the stock's own trailing volatility regime; an unusually large vol-adjusted move is typically a liquidity-driven overreaction that partially reverses over the next few days.

A short-run trading range that is compressing relative to its own longer-run range signals volatility contraction ahead of a breakout, so recent cumulative return should carry through more strongly once compression sets in.

Captures whether medium-term momentum is accelerating or decelerating relative to the longer-term trend, expressed in units of the stock's own long-run volatility so the acceleration reading is comparable across risk levels.

Price stretched away from its own short exponential average tends to snap back toward it; scaling the deviation by recent cumulative trading range adjusts for stocks that simply swing more from day to day.

Isolates earnings-power-supported price action from noise: a sudden short-horizon spike in raw share volume with no earnings-quality backing looks like speculative churn likely to fade, while the same spike in a high-earnings name looks like real information arrival.

A trading-range expansion that occurs in the same direction as the prevailing medium-term trend reflects broad participation and should continue, whereas the same range expansion against the trend is more likely noise.
A price trend accompanied by elevated relative volume reflects broader participation and conviction, so it should persist more than the same trend achieved on quiet volume (volume confirms trend).

Measures the skew of the recent daily-return distribution; a window dominated by one large outlier day relative to the rest of the distribution flags a crash-and-rebound or melt-up-and-cool pattern likely to partially reverse.

Tracks how quickly a stock's rolling price ceiling is rising, scaled by its typical daily range; a fast-rising high-water mark relative to normal trading noise signals a genuinely strengthening uptrend rather than one isolated high print.

A Sortino-style momentum measure that scales cumulative return by realized downside volatility only; a trend built mostly on down-day turbulence (capitulation-driven) is less trustworthy than the same cumulative return earned with little downside volatility.

prompt:
You are proposing quantitative factor expressions for US large-cap equities.

Universe and data
- S&P 500 point-in-time constituents, roughly 500 names per day.
- Daily bars only, plus point-in-time quarterly fundamentals stamped from the
  report date. Every field is referenced with a leading `$`:
    $open $high $low $close $adj_close $volume $dollar_volume $return
    $roa $roe $operating_margin $leverage $asset_turnover
    $book_per_share $earnings_per_share $accrual_gap
  A bare name such as `close` is not a field and will be rejected.
- Execution convention: the signal is computed after the close of day T and the
  position is entered at the open of T+1.
- The window these factors are fitted and judged on runs from 2000 to 2013.
  Do not reason about anything later; you will never be shown a number from
  outside that window.

Syntax
- Operators are function calls: TS_MEAN, TS_STD, TS_MAX, TS_MIN, TS_RANK,
  TS_DELTA, TS_CORR, TS_COV, TS_SUM, TS_PRODUCT, TS_ARGMAX, TS_ARGMIN,
  TS_DECAY_LINEAR, EMA, DELAY, DELTA, RANK, ZSCORE, CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE,
  CS_DEMEAN, IF, IF_ELSE, MIN, MAX, ABS, SIGN, LOG, LN, SQRT, POWER, BOUND,
  COUNT.
- Lookback windows must be positive integer literals, e.g. TS_MEAN($close, 21).
- Guard every division with a small epsilon: `/ (TS_STD($close, 21) + 1e-8)`.
- Well-formed example: -RANK(TS_CORR(RANK($close), RANK($volume), 5))

Hard limits every proposal must satisfy, or it is rejected before it is scored
- at most 200 characters
- at most 5 distinct `$fields`
- at most 4 free numeric constants (lookback windows and
  the 1e-8 epsilon guard do not count)
- expression tree depth at most 6
- must not share a complete sub-expression of 4 or more
  nodes with any published Alpha101 formula, or with any factor already in the
  archive. Restating a published alpha is the one thing that is always rejected.
- must cover at least 90% of the panel
- absolute rank correlation below 0.80 against every archive member

Output
- Return valid JSON only, matching the supplied JSON schema. No prose outside it.

Working memory: rules written after earlier rounds on this island, oldest first. Apply them.
  1. RANK($roa * $asset_turnover) still hit rho 0.907 against RANK($roa) alone — multiplying two DuPont-related fundamentals doesn't decorrelate from either. Treat roa/roe/operating_margin/asset_turnover as one correlated cluster; vary the non-fundamental side of the expression instead.
  2. archive_subtree caught more than window edits this round: swapping one OHLC field (open for close) in an otherwise-identical ratio, swapping one fundamental leaf in a two-term rank spread, and wrapping an archived payload in LN() all still shared most of the parent's nodes. Change an inner operator or structure, not a single field/fundamental/wrapper.
  3. A 63-day range ratio survived a denominator swap and an added vol-scaling term but still hit rho 0.916 against the archived version (TS_MEAN($high/$low,63)/TS_STD($return,63) vs TS_MEAN(($high-$low)/$open,63)). Changing which price anchors a range ratio isn't enough to decorrelate it — change the window or the core comparison.
  4. Both crossover_not_a_fusion rejects this round donated only ABS($return) (2 nodes) from a TS_CORR(ABS($return), $volume, 21)-shaped parent, short of the minimum. Donate a larger structural chunk of that parent, not just the ABS($return) leaf.
  5. Crossover fusions on TS_CORR(ABS($return), $volume, w) fail as 'not a fusion' (only 2 shared nodes) whenever $volume is swapped for another field or the pair gets re-wrapped as CS_RANK(fundamental)*TS_RANK(...) — keep ABS($return) and $volume both intact in the shared subtree and only vary w or add an outer wrapper.
  6. ~252-day windows fail coverage at 0.82-0.88 even on pure OHLC fields, not just fundamentals: TS_MEAN($open,63)-TS_MEAN($open,252) over TS_MEAN($high,252)-TS_MEAN($low,252) scored 0.857 coverage — treat ~1yr windows as broadly off-limits regardless of field.
  7. This round's standout accept (11.707) normalizes a close-low position by TS_RANK($dollar_volume,5)+eps rather than raw/derived dollar_volume — try more denominators built on TS_RANK(volume) instead of the volume level itself.
  8. Wrapping $dollar_volume in a ratio (($high/$low)/($dollar_volume+eps)) still hit rho 0.988 against plain TS_MEAN($dollar_volume,21) — a light numerator wrapper does not decorrelate raw dollar_volume; it dominates almost any expression it sits in.
  9. The (price - TS_MIN(w))/(TS_MAX(w)-TS_MIN(w)) position-in-range family failed correlation twice more (rho 0.875, 0.935) from window-only changes (5/21/42) and from a same-shape high-side reframing — saturated across windows, not just at the literal duplicate.
  10. RANK($earnings_per_share) - RANK(TS_DELTA($dollar_volume,63)) scored 4.053, beating the best fundamental-fundamental rank spread on file (3.405) — fundamental-minus-volume-delta spreads look more promising than pure fundamental-fundamental ones; try more.
  11. -TS_DELTA($open,3)/(TS_MEAN($high,21)-TS_MEAN($low,21)+eps) missed cheap_screen narrowly (|t| 0.93 vs 1.00) — short (3d) open-deltas normalized by 21d range are close to signal; retry with a CS_RANK wrapper or adjacent window before dropping the shape.
  12. ($open - DELAY($low or $high,1)) constructions keep colliding with Alpha101-family archive members (5-node overlap) — this shape is largely exhausted; only reuse it fused with a clearly distinct fundamental or volume leg.

For each proposal give a one-line economic rationale: what mechanism would make
this predict returns. "It is a momentum variant" is not a mechanism.
